The Hermes III designation originally applied to the Draconis Combine's HER-4K variant of the Hermes II, but Luthien Armor Works' extensive post-Jihad upgrades have effectively created a new chassis bearing the same name. Built from salvaged HER-4K frames recovered from militias and scrapyards across the Combine, these modernized 'Mechs incorporate advanced technology that transforms the aging scouts into capable contemporary reconnaissance platforms.

Luthien Armor Works' involvement reflects the DCMS's urgent need to reconstitute its reconnaissance forces following the devastating losses of the Jihad. Rather than waiting for new construction, LAW's engineers developed comprehensive refit packages that could rapidly return damaged Hermes III frames to frontline service while dramatically improving their combat capabilities.

The upgraded Hermes III retains the original's role as a heavy scout and skirmisher while significantly enhancing its combat potential. The refitted snub-nose PPCs provide effective firepower within 270 meters, offering pilots a measure of parity against contemporary medium 'Mechs without the range disadvantages of the original's large lasers. The sacrifice of the traditional flamer for an additional hand actuator improves the 'Mech's ability to manipulate objects during extended operations, a practical consideration for reconnaissance units operating far from supply lines.

Advanced electronics distinguish the modernized Hermes III from its predecessor. The proven Irian E.A.R. communications system receives upgrades including Guardian ECM integration and C3 slave capability, allowing the 'Mech to coordinate with Combine tactical networks while providing electronic countermeasures protection. The Cat's Eyes targeting computer enhances accuracy, partially compensating for the snub-nose PPCs' reduced effective range compared to standard particle cannons.

The chassis itself receives attention, with an Irian-Ost-LAW hybrid frame incorporating improvements developed through the partnership between the original manufacturer and its Combine counterpart. A GM 240 XL engine maintains the design's mobility while Samarkand Royal Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides improved protection without excessive weight penalties.

The original Hermes III emerged during the First Succession War when Ostmann Industries' Kuritan branch recognized the potential in Hermes II chassis imported under the Concord of Kapteyn. Their engineers transformed these Free Worlds League scouts into energy-focused strikers that eliminated ammunition dependency, creating a variant that proved popular enough to receive its own designation despite being built on the same forty-ton frame.

The Jihad's devastation of DCMS reconnaissance forces created urgent demand for capable scout platforms. Rather than waiting for new construction to fill the gap, Luthien Armor Works recovered damaged and abandoned HER-4K frames from across the Combine, developing comprehensive upgrade packages that could rapidly return these veterans to service. The New Samarkand Refit Facility became the primary center for this work, processing salvaged chassis and upgrading them to contemporary standards.

The upgraded Hermes III received its first combat test on Mualang in 3084 during a Ghost Bear incursion. Elements of the First Sword of Light's Third Battalion deployed several HER-6Ks on a flanking maneuver that surprised the Ninth Provisional Garrison Cluster, demonstrating the modernized design's reconnaissance and fire support capabilities. The engagement marked the end of serious Ghost Bear offensive operations on the world.

Subsequent deployments during the Second Combine-Dominion War further validated the design. At Trondheim in 3100, Hermes IIIs from the Eleventh Ghost were among the first 'Mechs to reach the ground during heavily contested combat drops, using their C3 integration to direct fire support while still descending. Luthien Armor Works continues developing new variants, with the HER-7K representing their latest effort to create the definitive version of this venerable chassis.

The two machines that became the Ugly Stepsisters began as scrap. Around 3138, technicians working for what would later be organized as Team Godmother cannibalized three very different donor 'Mechs, a Hunchback dating to the early 3050s, an early-production Legionnaire, and a Clan-built Pinion, and recombined their salvageable sections into a matched pair of fifty-ton hybrids. The result honored none of the original designs and instead followed the team's theatrical conceit, a Solaris dueling stable themed around the Cinderella story, with the two brawlers cast as the wicked stepsisters Anastasia and Drizella.

Team Godmother was a newcomer to the Solaris VII circuit, assembled and trained for the 3146 Royal Fantasy Tournament after several quieter years of preparation. The stable carried no permanent owner of record and was widely understood to be backed by the Federated Suns, fielding three contracted independent gladiators rather than a roster of house pilots. On a world where reputation is won in the arena rather than on the battlefield, the Stepsisters provided the team's heavy muscle, deliberately unlovely machines built to punish opponents who underestimated cobbled-together salvage.

The Huntsman was originally developed by Clan Diamond Shark as a totemic OmniMech honoring their namesake predator, but before the design could enter full production, Clan Nova Cat won exclusive manufacturing rights through a Trial of Possession driven by the fierce rivalry between the two Clans' Merchant Castes. Entering production in 3049, the fifty-ton Huntsman quickly became the premier medium OmniMech of Clan Nova Cat, exemplifying the flexibility and adaptability that defined the OmniMech concept. Khan Severen Leoux contracted Clan Cloud Cobra's Brim Ironworks facility for additional manufacturing, ensuring sufficient production to equip Nova Cat frontline units in time for Operation Revival.

First encountered by Inner Sphere forces during the Battle of Luthien in 3052, a Draconis Combine intelligence officer designated the OmniMech "Nobori-nin" after the distinctive dorsal fin projection reminded him of the banners feudal samurai wore on their backs. The Huntsman has since spread well beyond its Nova Cat origins, serving with multiple Clans and finding renewed production under the Clan Protectorate on Asellus Australis.

Sturdy and stable, the Huntsman dedicates nearly half its mass to pod space, granting MechWarriors exceptional flexibility in loadout configuration. Built on a Mynx Type Medium Endo Steel chassis and powered by a 250-rated Consolidated extralight fusion engine, the design achieves a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Five fixed Northrup Starlifters jump jets provide a one-hundred-fifty-meter leap capability, offsetting what some warriors consider a middling ground speed for a medium OmniMech. Nine tons of Alpha Compound ferro-fibrous armor provide protection comparable to many heavier designs, contributing to the Huntsman's reputation as the equal in raw survivability of numerous heavy 'Mechs taking the field.

The Primary configuration demonstrates the Huntsman's versatility with a broad weapons mix spanning all engagement ranges. An Ultra autocannon/2 and Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-10 provide long-range suppression, while four extended-range medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 deliver devastating close-range firepower. An active probe, TAG spotting laser, and anti-missile system round out the electronics suite, making the Prime configuration an exceptionally capable scout and skirmisher. The twenty-three and a half tons of available pod space allow configurations ranging from heavy fire support to dedicated brawler loadouts, though warriors accustomed to faster medium designs occasionally chafe at the Huntsman's more measured pace.

The Huntsman's origins lie in the intense commercial rivalry between the Merchant Castes of Clans Nova Cat and Diamond Shark, whose competition for resources and trade opportunities was among the fiercest in the Clan Homeworlds prior to Operation Revival. When the Nova Cats successfully trialed for exclusive production rights to the promising new Diamond Shark OmniMech, it became a long-standing point of irritation that their totemic shark design had become a quintessential Nova Cat machine. Khan Severen Leoux wisely contracted Clan Cloud Cobra's Brim Ironworks to supplement Nova Cat production, preserving the Clan's own industrial capacity for other priorities.

The Huntsman first saw combat against Inner Sphere forces during Operation Revival, where it appeared in the ranks of the 119th Nova Cat Striker Cluster at the Battle of Luthien. Throughout the Clan Invasion, the design remained almost exclusively a Nova Cat asset, prized for its flexibility across diverse opponents and battlefield conditions. In the years following the invasion, however, Clan Diamond Shark finally reclaimed the right to produce their totemic design, while Clan Cloud Cobra's long manufacturing partnership led to the sharing of schematics with Clan Star Adder. By the outbreak of the Jihad, multiple Clans fielded significant numbers of the Huntsman.

The Word of Blake Jihad proved devastating for Huntsman production. The Nova Cat facilities on Irece and Avon were both destroyed in 3071, severely curtailing the supply of new chassis. When a significant portion of the Clan Nova Cat Touman joined the Republic of the Sphere after the Jihad, Huntsmans began appearing in Republic Armed Forces livery, a sight that raised eyebrows among observers who recognized the distinctly Clan design in recent RAF operations.

The Second Combine-Dominion War further depleted Nova Cat Huntsman numbers, as combat losses outpaced the Clan's diminished ability to replace them. The establishment of the Clan Protectorate brought renewed hope for the design, with Clan Protectorate Arms on Asellus Australis placing the Huntsman back into production for use by the descendants of both Nova Cat and Sea Fox, serving as a symbol of new cooperation within the Protectorate. Meanwhile, Brim Ironworks has maintained continuous production throughout these upheavals, ensuring the Huntsman remains a common sight on battlefields across the Inner Sphere and Clan territories alike.

The Hyena was developed by Vining Engineering and Salvage Team (VEST) on Solaris VII as a purpose-built SalvageMech, first offered for sale in 3066. The design addressed a persistent problem in battlefield recovery: accessing wrecked BattleMechs in terrain too rough for conventional salvage vehicles. VEST, already well-regarded as masters of BattleMech innovation on the Game World, designed the Hyena to be fast enough to keep pace with combat elements while carrying the equipment necessary to recover even the heaviest downed BattleMechs.

The design quickly became the standard by which other SalvageMechs were measured, with buyers ranging from mercenary groups and Great House militaries to Periphery nations. Surviving Hyenas remain highly prized assets, and the design's reputation for effective battlefield recovery is unmatched among purpose-built salvage platforms.

Built on a 55-ton IndustrialMech chassis, the Hyena's defining feature is its comprehensive salvage equipment suite. A pair of rear-mounted lift hoists give the design the ability to lift over 100 tons when working in concert with the chassis's industrial triple-strength myomer, enabling it to handle even assault-class BattleMechs without assistance. The sophisticated salvage arm mounted in the right arm provides the fine manipulation needed for delicate component extraction and precision work that lift hoists alone cannot accomplish.

The CoreTek 275 fusion engine provides a top speed of 84 kilometers per hour, comparable to medium-class BattleMechs and fast enough that the design does not require a support escort to keep pace with combat formations. Environmental sealing protects the crew in hazardous conditions ranging from chemical contamination to hard vacuum, allowing recovery operations in environments that would sideline unprotected salvage vehicles.

Seven and a half tons of Corning 84 industrial-grade armor provides reasonable protection for a non-combat design, while a single Defiance B3S small laser mounted in the center torso offers minimal self-defense against infantry and opportunistic scavengers. The Hyena trades offensive capability almost entirely for recovery utility, a compromise that has proven highly effective on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.

The Hyena's origins trace to the arena culture of Solaris VII, where VEST founder Dr. David Vining recognized that recovering damaged BattleMechs from the Game World's varied combat environments demanded a purpose-built machine rather than adapted construction equipment. Founded in 3047, VEST quickly earned a reputation for engineering innovation in BattleMech salvage and repair, and the Hyena represented their most ambitious project.

The first Hyena prototypes were converted from surplus Kintaro BattleMechs, retaining much of the donor chassis's structure while replacing all weapons systems with specialized salvage equipment. These two prototypes demonstrated that a BattleMech-based salvage platform could access terrain conventional recovery vehicles could not, and could do so at speeds that kept pace with combat formations. The concept proved so successful that VEST developed a dedicated production chassis, the HYN-4A, which entered the market in 3066.

The Hyena's commercial success was immediate but tragically brief. Every unit from VEST's first and only production run sold quickly, going to mercenary commands, Great House militaries, and Periphery nations. VEST provided a unit at reduced cost to Skibinski's Salvage, a specialized recovery team, as a traveling demonstration of the design's capabilities. During the Jihad, Hyena-equipped salvage teams frequently outpaced competing recovery crews to battle sites, stripping valuable components from destroyed machines before more cumbersome vehicles could even reach the area.

The Word of Blake's occupation of Solaris VII proved devastating for VEST's production capacity. In 3072, Blakist forces destroyed both surviving Kintaro-based prototypes and VEST's primary production facilities in the city of Xolara. Undeterred, VEST engineers working from improvised workshops managed to produce three ICE-powered variants for the Solaris Home Defense League, demonstrating remarkable adaptability under wartime conditions. With the Hyena unavailable through normal channels, competitors such as the Jabberwocky began attracting former prospective customers.

Following the Jihad, VEST pursued recovery rather than capitulation. The company issued an initial public offering on the Lyran Alliance Stock Exchange in 3079, raising an estimated 600 million kroner to rebuild facilities and recruit new staff. Several major corporations, including Earthwerks, approached VEST with offers to license or produce the Hyena design, though Dr. Vining and his team repeatedly declined these overtures, preferring to rebuild on their own terms rather than sell from a position of weakness.

The Icarus II was the first homegrown BattleMech design to be mass-produced by the Free Worlds League. Introduced in 2518 by Corean Enterprises, the design represented a substantial upgrade of the earlier Icarus prototype, incorporating newly acquired jump jet technology that prompted Corean to add the "II" designation. Originally conceived as a light attack and cavalry 'Mech to complement the massive Mackie and support heavy Marik tanks, the Icarus II filled both support and strike roles within the Free Worlds League Military for centuries.

At its production peak, the design was manufactured on four separate worlds, and its low-cost simplicity earned it a loyal following among FWLM commanders. Though eventually overtaken by newer medium designs, the Icarus II has proven remarkably resilient, returning to production multiple times across its long service history and earning a reputation as one of the Inner Sphere's most enduring BattleMech lineages.

At forty tons, the Icarus II occupied the lower end of the medium-weight classification. A DAV 160 fusion engine provided a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, more than adequate when the design was introduced but increasingly outpaced as BattleMech technology matured. The Icarus 81 jump jets compensated for this limitation, allowing the 'Mech to leap up to one hundred and twenty meters and fight effectively in urban environments and broken terrain.

The primary weapon is an Imperator-B autocannon/10, a heavy main gun for a medium chassis that provided excellent range and hitting power. Two Diverse Optics Type 2 medium lasers and a single Diverse Optics Type 10 small laser supplemented the autocannon, giving the pilot options at multiple engagement ranges. Seven and a half tons of StarSlab armor provided adequate protection for the design's intended cavalry role, though the emphasis on firepower over armor became a liability as the Icarus II was increasingly pressed into strike and defensive assignments.

Late in its original service life, the Icarus II was typically paired with faster scouts in light attack lances. A fast scout would seek out the enemy, and then a trio of Icarus IIs would attack the designated target using concentrated autocannon fire. While effective, the 'Mech's limited speed meant it could not escape when overmatched.

shared: The Ice Ferret, designated Fenris by Inner Sphere forces, is a forty-five ton medium OmniMech first produced in 2948 by Clan Ice Hellion at their W-7 Facilities on Tranquil. Originally designated the Wolf Hunter, the design was conceived as Clan Ice Hellion's answer to the formidable Timber Wolf OmniMech fielded by Clan Wolf. Emphasizing speed and firepower over raw tonnage, the Ice Hellion warriors envisioned a fast hunter-killer capable of challenging the pride of the Wolf touman. The design's initial configurations proved lackluster, however, and Clan Wolf warriors began systematically challenging Ice Hellions for possession of the OmniMech through Trials of Possession. Within five years, the Wolves had claimed eighty percent of the Ice Hellion's Wolf Hunter inventory, including the production facility itself. Renaming the design after the ice ferret (the only natural predator of the ice hellion on the planet Hector) Clan Wolf refined the configurations and transformed the chassis into one of the most versatile medium OmniMechs in their touman.

The Ice Ferret is built on a lightweight endo steel chassis powered by a massive 360-rated XL engine, propelling the forty-five ton OmniMech to speeds of nearly one hundred thirty kilometers per hour. This exceptional speed makes the Ice Ferret one of the fastest medium 'Mechs in any Clan arsenal, though it comes at the cost of pod space, the engine alone accounts for roughly one-third of the design's total mass. Protected by seven and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor, the Ice Ferret carries nearly the maximum protection possible for its weight class, giving it surprising resilience for a design built around speed.

The chassis mounts twelve fixed double heat sinks and carries nine and a half tons of pod space, enabling a wide variety of mission loadouts. In its Primary configuration, the Ice Ferret balances long-range striking power with reconnaissance capability, mounting an ER PPC for engagements at extended range, supplemented by a Streak SRM-2 and ER small laser for close defense. An active probe supplements the chassis's already superior sensor suite, allowing MechWarriors to detect hidden units, a capability that has proven decisive in numerous reconnaissance operations. This combination of speed, sensors, and flexible armament makes the Ice Ferret equally effective as a scout, striker, or headhunter.

The Ice Ferret's origins lie in Clan Ice Hellion's ambitious attempt to challenge Clan Wolf's dominance during the mid-twenty-ninth century. Designated the Wolf Hunter upon its debut in 2948, the OmniMech was intended to demonstrate Ice Hellion technological prowess and provide their warriors with a platform capable of defeating the vaunted Timber Wolf in single combat. The Ice Hellions' carries proved premature, their initial weapon configurations failed to exploit the chassis's potential, and Wolf warriors found the design more noteworthy for its promise than its performance.

Tired of constant Hellion provocations, Clan Wolf units began challenging Ice Hellion possessors of Wolf Hunters through formal Trials of Possession. The resulting campaigns were devastating for Clan Ice Hellion, which lost eighty percent of its Wolf Hunter inventory over five years, including the production facility on Tranquil. The Wolves renamed the OmniMech after the ice ferret, the sole natural predator of the ice hellion species on the planet Hector, a calculated insult that soured other Clans on the design and dampened interest in acquiring it through further Trials. The Ice Hellions maintained a large number of their remaining Wolf Hunters in their touman throughout their existence, refusing to adopt the new designation.

Under Wolf stewardship, the Ice Ferret's configurations were refined and the design became a cornerstone of the Wolf touman's medium weight forces. Many configurations revolve on a single long-range weapon backed by several smaller short-range batteries, giving MechWarriors a distinct advantage over speed-centered designs that typically rely on slews of light short-range weapons. Following the Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere and the subsequent Refusal War, the Wolves-in-Exile established a secondary production line at Wolf Clan Site 3 on Arc-Royal, ensuring continued supply for their forces operating in the Inner Sphere. The Ice Ferret saw extensive service with the exiled Wolves and their allies, the Kell Hounds, throughout the late thirty-first and early thirty-second centuries.

The design's few remaining Homeworld production facilities were destroyed during the chaotic fighting of the Wars of Reaving, leading to the Ice Ferret being phased out of use among Homeworld Clans and gradually replaced by the Viper. In the Inner Sphere, however, the design persisted. The Arc-Royal production line was destroyed during the fall of Arc-Royal in 3146, when defenders employed two Stars of Ice Ferrets in a desperate rearguard action against advancing Clan Jade Falcon forces, deliberately scuttling the factory rather than allowing it to be taken as isorla. By the time the Falcons destroyed the last defending Ice Ferret, they were left with a burning factory and no salvageable production equipment.

Production subsequently shifted to Assault Tech Industries on Donegal, where the design continues to serve with Clan Wolf-in-Exile forces. Numerous Ice Ferrets were also present among the Kell Hounds before their disappearance into the Periphery, and the design has proliferated to other factions through battlefield salvage, with Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Hell's Horses both fielding examples acquired through conquest. The Ice Ferret's combination of speed, armor, and flexible pod configurations has ensured its continued relevance despite the loss of multiple production facilities over the centuries.

Twin Lord's Light 5 snub-nose PPCs replace the original large lasers, providing effective medium-range firepower with improved damage potential at the cost of maximum engagement distance. text.deployment: Luthien Armor Works' newest Hermes III variant addresses longstanding criticisms of the design's speed relative to dedicated light scouts. A supercharger provides burst acceleration capability, while a Bloodhound probe and Angel ECM offer formidable electronic warfare capabilities superior to the standard Guardian suite. text.overview:
The Highlander is one of the most iconic assault BattleMechs in the history of the Inner Sphere, first entering service with the Star League Defense Force in 2592. Designed by StarCorps Industries as a dedicated city and installation defender, the ninety-ton design combined a versatile weapons mix, heavy ferro-fibrous armor protection, and an unusual feature for an assault chassis: jump jets that granted it tactical mobility unmatched by its peers. This agility proved so effective that within decades of its introduction, nearly every Regular and Royal Army BattleMech regiment featured Highlanders in their ranks.

Perhaps more than any other single design, the Highlander is defined by the infamous "Highlander Burial", a death-from-above attack in which the 'Mech leaps onto a lighter opponent and literally drives it into the ground. So popular was this devastating tactic that StarCorps reengineered the Highlander's legs specifically to withstand repeated such attacks, transforming a desperation move into a signature combat technique feared across every battlefield in the Inner Sphere and beyond.
text.capabilities:
The Highlander carries a weapons mix optimized for ranged engagements that remains effective when ranges close. The primary weapon of the original HGN-732 is an M-7 Gauss rifle capable of delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range, backed by a Holly LRM-20 launcher for sustained long-range fire support. At closer distances, a Holly SRM-6 rack and a pair of Harmon Starclass medium lasers provide significant short-range firepower. Two tons of ammunition for each launcher system and the Gauss rifle provide excellent battlefield endurance, while CASE protects the MechWarrior from catastrophic ammunition explosions.

Fifteen and a half tons of Grumman-3 ferro-fibrous armor make the Highlander exceptionally well protected for its class, while three HildCo Model 10 jump jets grant it a mobility advantage that most assault 'Mechs cannot match. This combination of firepower, protection, and mobility allows the Highlander to control engagement ranges, pursue fleeing opponents, and execute the feared Highlander Burial with devastating effect. The design's relatively low heat output allows pilots to maintain a near-continuous barrage, though sustained use of all weapons systems simultaneously still demands thermal discipline.
text.deployment: This custom configuration replaces the standard 732's weapons suite with an ER PPC, a prototype Streak SRM-6, twin Medium Pulse Lasers, and a pair of LRM-15 missile launchers. Fourteen double heat sinks manage the substantially increased thermal output. The modification serves as a significant departure from the original Highlander weapons philosophy, trading the Gauss rifle's long-range precision for the ER PPC's sustained energy output while maintaining robust missile capability at all ranges.
text.battleHistory:
Designed for the Star League Defense Force in 2592, the Highlander was an instant success with both Regular and Royal regiments. Its wide variety of weapons and jump jets allowed it to take on any situation, and the design rapidly became one of the most common assault 'Mechs in the SLDF order of battle. The Highlander saw extensive service through the final decades of the Star League era, and many accompanied General Aleksandr Kerensky on the Exodus, where Clan scientists would eventually upgrade surviving chassis into the formidable Highlander IIC using advanced Clan technology.

The Succession Wars devastated Highlander production in the Inner Sphere. StarCorps' factory on Son Hoa was destroyed toward the end of the Second Succession War, driving the original HGN-732 to virtual extinction. An agreement between Hollis Incorporated and StarCorps to rebuild destroyed chassis from scratch using readily available technology produced the downgraded HGN-733, which Hollis continued to custom-build on Corey until the Fourth Succession War when the licensing arrangement was revoked. By the mid-3030s, StarCorps had managed to restart limited production on Son Hoa, producing barely a dozen new 'Mechs per year.

Throughout the Succession Wars, ComStar secretly maintained a large stock of original Highlanders inherited from the Star League. During the War of 3039, ComStar provided both HGN-733s and a few advanced HGN-732s to the Draconis Combine, shocking Lyran forces who encountered what they believed to be extinct Star League-era technology. The Northwind Highlanders also maintained a disproportionate number of operational Highlanders through the Succession Wars, many with original Star League-era components, and their skill with the Highlander Burial became legendary.

By 3057, StarCorps' Son Hoa factory had returned to full production, producing original-specification HGN-732 Highlanders for Lyran units of the Federated Commonwealth. The FedCom Civil War spurred the development of multiple advanced variants, including the urban-combat focused HGN-734 and the ComStar-enhanced HGN-736. The HGN-734's debut in 3062 also had an unexpected civilian legacy: the production changeover left a surplus of older-specification components, which StarCorps repurposed to create the St. Florian FireMech, one of the most advanced IndustrialMechs introduced since the fall of the Star League. Post-Civil War production continued to diversify, with the HGN-738 introducing Heavy Gauss Rifle technology and the experimental HGN-641-X-2 pushing the boundaries of what the venerable chassis could accommodate.

The Word of Blake Jihad severely disrupted Highlander production when Blakist forces attacked the Son Hoa factories in 3074, rendering them temporarily inoperable. Meanwhile, Clan Wolf had established its own Highlander legacy on Weingarten, converting salvaged Inner Sphere chassis into Highlander IICs at the W-7 Facilities, an operation that would eventually pass to Clan Hell's Horses when they captured the planet in 3142. Production of new Inner Sphere variants eventually resumed on Son Hoa, and designs such as the HGN-740 continued to emerge well into the Dark Age. The Highlander's long and distinguished service record, combined with its association with the famed Northwind Highlanders mercenary brigade, has cemented its place as one of the most recognized and respected assault 'Mechs in the history of mechanized warfare.

text.overview: The Hitotsume Kozo is a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech introduced in 3136 by Luthien Armor Works on New Samarkand. Conceived during the Draconis Combine's unofficial cultural rebirth, LAW engineers designed the chassis as a stylized homage to ancient Japanese samurai, channeling the aggressive close-combat philosophy that had come to define a new generation of Combine war machines. Similar in doctrine to the Rokurokubi, the Hitotsume Kozo fills the role of a medium striker capable of devastating enemies at range before closing to deliver punishing melee attacks. Initially unpopular among front-line formations due to its demanding heat management, the design ultimately earned a fearsome reputation in the hands of the Ghost Regiments and other aggressive units within the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery.
text.capabilities:
The Hitotsume Kozo's primary weapon is a shoulder-mounted Lord's Light 3 heavy particle projection cannon, capable of delivering devastating fire at range while building the heat necessary to activate the 'Mech's Triple Strength Myomer. A pair of Diverse Optics Type 20X extended-range medium lasers provide supplementary firepower from the left arm, while a stylized hatchet (fashioned to resemble an ancient Japanese double-ended sickle) gives the design its signature melee capability. When the myomer bundles reach optimal operating temperature, the Hitotsume Kozo transforms from a moderately fast skirmisher into a terrifyingly quick close-quarters killer.

A Hermes 330 XL engine provides respectable speed for a medium 'Mech, while four Icarus 81 jump jets grant tactical flexibility on broken terrain. The chassis mounts an impressive fourteen and a half tons of New Samarkand Teppeki hardened armor, granting exceptional resilience against ballistic and physical attacks at the cost of additional weight. This protection philosophy reflects the design's intended role: close with the enemy and endure return fire while delivering melee strikes.

The Hitotsume Kozo's greatest weakness is its challenging heat management. Only twelve double heat sinks struggle to dissipate the output of its energy weapons, forcing pilots to carefully manage their firing patterns. In inexperienced hands, the 'Mech can quickly overheat and shut down at the worst possible moment, a vulnerability that contributed to its initial unpopularity among conventional formations.
text.deployment: Debuting in 3139 on the King of the Mountain arena circuit on Solaris VII, the HKZ-1FM is a custom aftermarket modification that replaces the standard hatchet with a large vibroblade styled to resemble a traditional katana. The hardened armor skirting has been stripped in favor of lighter conventional armor, shedding weight and significantly improving the 'Mech's speed and agility at the cost of ballistic protection. The engine, weaponry, and electronic systems remain to Combine factory specifications. This combination of enhanced melee lethality and improved maneuverability makes the HKZ-1FM a crowd favorite in arena combat, though its reduced armor would be a serious liability in sustained battlefield engagements.
text.battleHistory:
The Hitotsume Kozo emerged during the turbulent 3130s, a period when the Draconis Combine experienced an unofficial cultural renaissance that deeply influenced military procurement. Luthien Armor Works, already producing the Rokurokubi and other culturally-inspired designs, developed the Hitotsume Kozo as a heavier complement to their existing lineup of Japanese-styled BattleMechs. Named after a mythological one-eyed dwarf from ancient Terran folklore, the design entered production at LAW's New Samarkand facility in 3136.

The 'Mech's early service history was marked by rejection from mainstream DCMS formations. Front-line commanders considered the design too temperamental, its heat management too demanding, and its advanced systems too difficult to maintain for conventional units. The Procurement Department redirected production to the Ghost Regiments and other formations considered expendable by the Combine's military establishment. This decision proved serendipitous, enthusiastic officers and the yakuza-samurai who populated these units embraced the Hitotsume Kozo's aggressive design philosophy wholeheartedly.

Through extensive practice and raiding operations, Ghost Regiment warriors transformed the Hitotsume Kozo into an efficient killing machine. Paired with Rokurokubis and other fast close-quarters 'Mechs, Hitotsume Kozos provided ranged cover fire before closing to deliver devastating melee attacks. One notable engagement on the world of Mara demonstrated the design's effectiveness when a mixed Ghost company assaulted a fortified bunker network. Five Hitotsume Kozos blasted distant fortifications with their heavy PPCs before sprinting forward to wade into the defensive complex, using their hatchets to cut through the remaining defenders and breach the bunker line for the assault force.

By the ilClan era, the Hitotsume Kozo had firmly established itself within the DCMS, with LAW continuing production at New Samarkand. The design's reputation had evolved considerably from its inauspicious beginnings, earning grudging respect even among formations that had initially rejected it. The introduction of the HKZ-1P variant provided a more accessible option for conventional units, while the original HKZ-1F remained the preferred choice of veteran warriors who had mastered its demanding heat curve.

text.overview: The Hollander was introduced in 3054, born from Coventry Metal Works' response to a Federated Commonwealth commission seeking a light 'Mech capable of matching Clan firepower at range. The AFFC had evaluated numerous designs featuring PPCs and LRM systems, but Coventry's unorthodox proposal to mount a full-sized Gauss rifle on a thirty-five-ton chassis won the contract. Though the resulting design required significant compromises in armor, speed, and secondary armament, the Hollander delivered on its promise of providing Inner Sphere commanders with a light hunter-killer capable of destroying enemy light 'Mechs with a single devastating shot at extreme range. Cheap to produce and effective in its specialized role, the Hollander saw widespread adoption across Lyran and FedCom-employed units, with prominent mercenary commands also receiving shipments. The design's success spawned several variant lines attempting to address its inherent limitations while preserving its core philosophy.
text.capabilities:
Essentially a walking cannon, the Hollander's design is as extreme as it is straightforward. The entire chassis and structure were developed expressly to carry a single Poland Main Model A Gauss rifle, with every other consideration subordinated to that goal. Coventry engineers employed an endo-steel internal structure and ferro-fibrous armor to maximize weight savings, though even these advanced materials forced painful compromises elsewhere. The seven-ton Omni 175 standard engine limits the 'Mech to a top speed of just eighty-six kilometers per hour (comparable to a Clan heavy 'Mech) while only four tons of Lexington Limited ferro-fibrous armor leave the design dangerously vulnerable to return fire.

The Hollander carries no secondary weapons whatsoever, and its two tons of Gauss ammunition provide only sixteen shots before the MechWarrior is left completely defenseless. These limitations are accepted because the design excels at its intended role: delivering crippling long-range fire from the battlefield's edge. Heavily reinforced legs fitted with recoil compensators and support hydraulics allow the 'Mech to fire accurately even at a full run. So long as ammunition holds out and the pilot maintains standoff distance, the Hollander poses a genuine threat to targets well above its weight class.
text.deployment: A Dark Age-era field refit emerging around 3121, this variant was inspired by the success of the Hollander III program. Older Hollanders are retrofitted with a light Gauss rifle and a supercharger, trading the original weapon's raw stopping power for improved survivability through the ability to make rapid entrances and exits from combat. The modification gained popularity among mercenary and garrison units seeking to modernize aging Hollander chassis without the expense of acquiring entirely new designs.
text.battleHistory:
The Hollander emerged from the crucible of the Clan Invasion, with Coventry Metal Works receiving the AFFC contract in the early 3050s to produce a light 'Mech capable of matching Clan firepower at range. The design drew direct inspiration from the Kit Fox OmniMech's Gauss-armed configuration, and Coventry's engineers sought to replicate that capability on an affordable Inner Sphere chassis. Production began in 3054 at Coventry Metal Works on the Lyran world of Coventry.

The first production runs went directly to frontline units facing Clan Jade Falcon, with the Seventeenth Skye Rangers deploying them on Barcelona and the First Kearny Highlanders fielding them on Mogyorod. The design proved effective enough that shipments quickly expanded to additional Lyran, FedCom, and mercenary commands throughout the Clan Invasion era. Despite its battlefield success, the Hollander's severe limitations drove continuous development, with the BZK-G1 appearing in 3056 offering improved versatility.

The Lyran Alliance's eventual frustration with the design's shortcomings led to the commission of the Blitzkrieg as a more capable successor, though the Hollander's low cost ensured its continued service with garrison and second-line units. The Jihad devastated Coventry's production capacity, with the factory falling under contested Lyran control and active Hollander production ceasing.

The design found renewed relevance in the Dark Age when field technicians began converting older Hollanders to the BZK-G2 configuration, inspired by General Motors' Hollander III program on Kathil. These refits extended the venerable chassis' service life well into the thirty-second century, ensuring that the Hollander's distinctive silhouette remained a presence on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.

text.overview:
The Horned Owl, designated the Peregrine by Inner Sphere intelligence agencies, is a thirty-five-ton Clan light BattleMech first produced in 2835 by Clan Goliath Scorpion. Originally designed as a rugged submersible construction 'Mech intended to work alongside Water Elementals in the Pentagon Worlds, the Horned Owl was eventually rebuilt for combat during the early Homeworld settlement period. Its streamlined, non-threatening appearance made it well suited for garrison and security duties in civilian areas, a feature that frequently led observers to mistake it for a lightweight security 'Mech rather than the fully capable military platform it truly was.

Popular throughout the Clan Homeworlds and widely built for Provisional Garrison Clusters, the Horned Owl established itself as an effective harassing and dueling platform. Production expanded across multiple facilities over the centuries, with Clan Smoke Jaguar, Clan Ghost Bear, and the Rasalhague Dominion all eventually manufacturing their own versions of this versatile light design.
text.capabilities:
The Horned Owl is a harassing platform that lives and dies by its efficiency rather than raw firepower. Armed with a single Kolibri Delta Series large pulse laser mounted in the center torso and a Kolibri Omega Series medium pulse laser in each arm, the base design delivers devastatingly accurate fire capable of quickly dismantling other light 'Mechs. The stabilized center torso weapon allows the Horned Owl to maintain effective fire even at full speed, a critical advantage for a design that depends on mobility for survival.

Six jump jets distributed across the legs and side torsos provide a maximum jumping distance of one hundred and eighty meters, giving the Horned Owl excellent maneuverability across broken terrain. Five tons of ferro-fibrous armor offer adequate protection for a 'Mech of its weight class, though pilots must remain conscious of the design's limitations against heavier opponents. The all-energy weapon loadout of the base configuration ensures the Horned Owl can operate indefinitely without supply concerns, making it particularly well suited for extended patrol and deep raiding missions.

The Coriolis Class IIIb endo steel chassis and LightForce 210 engine drive the design to a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, striking a practical balance between speed and combat endurance that has kept the Horned Owl relevant across centuries of Clan warfare.
text.deployment: Produced by the Rasalhague Dominion at Alshain Weapons on Jarett beginning in 3132, the Horned Owl 6 returns to the pulse laser armament of the original design, carrying a large pulse laser and two medium pulse lasers. The six jump jets are traded for a targeting computer, sacrificing terrain mobility for dramatically improved weapons accuracy. The resulting ground-bound platform is optimized for open-field engagements where jumping capability is less critical than precise fire delivery, and has been widely exported to Inner Sphere powers including the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth.
text.battleHistory:
The Horned Owl traces its origins to the early settlement of the Clan Homeworlds, where Clan Goliath Scorpion designed it as a rugged submersible construction 'Mech built to work alongside Water Elementals. Produced at the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda, the design was eventually rebuilt for combat and became a common sight in Provisional Garrison Clusters throughout the Homeworlds. When Horned Owls first appeared in the Inner Sphere, military analysts viewed the streamlined design with confusion, comparing it to security or aquatic platforms and consistently underestimating its combat capability.

Clan Smoke Jaguar produced the missile-armed Horned Owl 2 variant at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, while the Horned Owl 3 emerged as an early Clan Ghost Bear effort to build the design for Inner Sphere deployment at Alshain Weapons on Jarett. In Clan trials, however, the Horned Owl was less successful against dedicated frontline designs, and the Smoke Jaguar and Goliath Scorpion offshoots used missiles to counteract this to middling effect. Modern Horned Owls have returned to their pulse laser roots, though later variants have yet to match the elegant simplicity of the original.

Following the annihilation of Clan Smoke Jaguar in 3060, the Goliath Scorpions moved quickly to seize the Abysmal continent on Huntress. This bold move netted them ProtoMech technical data and control of the long-neglected Abysmal Manufacturing Complex. The Scorpions extensively refitted the facility and introduced the radically redesigned Peregrine 4 in 3064, the first Horned Owl variant to employ Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Surprisingly, many Scorpion warriors did not receive the new design well. Instead, the Peregrine 4 found a ready market among the garrison Clusters of Clan Snow Raven's Kappa Galaxy, where its ATM launchers proved an effective counter to Clan Star Adder heavy laser platforms. The Snow Ravens also supplied Clan Blood Spirit with much-needed BattleMechs, and several Peregrines found their way into the Spirits' Iota Galaxy.

The all-energy Horned Owl 5, introduced in 3066, ironically proved more popular with Scorpion warriors than the ATM-armed variant. Its ability to operate indefinitely without ammunition resupply made it ideal for Seeker missions far from established supply lines, and it became a favorite of the newly formed Chi Galaxy. The Thirty-fifth Scorpion Hussars also received the variant, often fielding it in sparring matches with the Seventy-first Light Horse on Huntress.

The Rasalhague Dominion put the Horned Owl 6 into production at Alshain Weapons on Jarett in 3132 to serve its stillborn militia program. When the anticipated Sphere-wide conflagration in the wake of the HPG Blackout did not materialize, production was redirected into export, putting the Horned Owl into the thick of fighting against both the Falcons and the Draconis Combine. On Arc-Royal, dozens fell in Trials of Position against sibkin, while the Raven Alliance assigned the design to novice warriors in support of ProtoMechs. On the Draconis front, Horned Owls made life difficult for lighter designs, though they suffered against modern heavily armored opponents. The Horned Owl 7, dubbed the Shimafukuro and introduced around 3150, is a radical departure that sacrifices ground speed for enhanced jumping capability through a partial wing system, and despite being named for the Vega front has primarily seen action in riparian areas.

text.overview: Ramiel Bekker always loved unusual BattleMech history. One of his favorite tales was that of a trueborn warrior from a waning Bloodhouse who insisted on serving his front-line Galaxy in a salvaged Lyran Hunchback. Bekker recalled the story years later after Khan Alaric Ward gave him the run of Kali Yama Weapons. The Hunchback C is the antithesis of the Hunchback IIC used by other Clans, combining toughness and great ground speed with the heavy firepower of its autocannon.
text.notableUnits: Star Commander Matthew Wayne: Hulking, long-haired, dark-eyed, thick-bearded, and taciturn, Matthew Wayne hailed from an insignificant Bloodhouse with little political power. He served in the Ghost Bear’s Seventh Phalanx at the onset of the First Dominion-Combine War. He lost his OmniMech in one of the war’s deciding duels. This rendered him dezgra, and he was reassigned to a salvaged Hunchback. Refusing to accept his fate, Matthew heavily modified the ’Mech, hoping to claw back his honor.:br::tab:The Jihad would be his redemption when the Seventh Phalanx was sent to Pike IV. Matthew’s last opportunity for glory descended into fiasco when the Thirtieth PGC refused to aid the Phalanx. Though the Cluster was lost, Wayne led an epic fighting retreat saving what he could. Afterwards, the enraged Star Commander challenged the Thirtieth’s Star Colonel, but lost. Despite this, his actions garnered attention. He and his Hunchback were adopted by Delta Galaxy’s Seventy-Third Battle Cluster, which needed warriors experienced with fast ’Mechs for the assault on Thorin. Finally serving in a front-line Cluster, Wayne died gloriously on Thorin, clearing Blakists from the rubble of Fell’s Fort.

text.overview: The Hunchback was introduced in 2572 by Komiyaba/Nissan General Industries as a dedicated urban combat BattleMech, earning immediate respect during the brutal street fighting of the Reunification War. Designed as a medium-weight brawler optimized for close-quarters engagements, the Hunchback built its fearsome reputation around a single devastating autocannon capable of crippling opponents in a single well-placed volley. The design's proven reliability and straightforward maintenance ensured its survival through centuries of conflict. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere have produced the Hunchback in enormous numbers, with every Great House and most Periphery nations fielding them in significant quantities throughout the Succession Wars and beyond.
text.capabilities:
The Hunchback's combat doctrine revolves around its chassis-defining autocannon, mounted prominently in the right torso. In the standard HBK-4G configuration, the Kali Yama Big Bore Autocannon/20 consumes nearly a third of the 'Mech's total mass, delivering firepower that causes even assault-class MechWarriors to think twice about closing distance. A pair of arm-mounted medium lasers and a head-mounted small laser provide secondary firepower at short to medium range, ensuring the Hunchback remains dangerous even when ammunition runs low.

Ten tons of Starshield armor provides protection comparable to many heavy 'Mechs, allowing the Hunchback to absorb significant punishment during the close-range confrontations it seeks. However, this protection has led many MechWarriors to overestimate the design's durability; once the armor is breached, a direct hit to the autocannon or its ammunition storage can prove catastrophic. The thirteen single heat sinks manage the considerable waste heat with difficulty, requiring disciplined fire management to avoid shutdown.

The Hunchback's greatest tactical weakness is its modest speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, which relegates it to second-wave assault roles and leaves it vulnerable to faster 'Mechs that can maintain engagement range beyond its effective weapons envelope.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3133 during the Dark Age, the 6P builds upon the 5S chassis to serve as a direct fire support platform. A suite of light PPCs replaces the traditional autocannon armament, and a Radical Heat Sink System manages the considerable waste heat these weapons generate. This variant extends the Hunchback's effective engagement range well beyond its traditional close-quarters niche, enabling it to provide suppressive fire for advancing friendly forces from positions that would leave a standard Hunchback impotent.
text.battleHistory:
The Hunchback's origins trace to 2572, when Komiyaba/Nissan General Industries introduced the design to meet growing demand for dedicated urban combat platforms. The Reunification War provided the proving ground where the Hunchback first demonstrated its devastating close-range effectiveness, and the design quickly earned a reputation as one of the most dangerous 'Mechs to encounter in city fighting. During the Star League era, Diplass Technologies began additional production on Winter, further expanding the Hunchback's availability across the Inner Sphere.

The destruction of Komiyaba/Nissan's facilities on Nirasaki during the Succession Wars disrupted production until KaliYama Weapons Industries acquired the rights and established manufacturing on Kalidasa. The Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation particularly favored the design, whose all-or-nothing firepower suited their aggressive combat doctrines. The Free Worlds League emerged as the largest operator by the thirty-first century, benefiting directly from Kali Yama's domestic production. Throughout the Succession Wars, dwindling autocannon stocks forced technicians to develop the various Swayback configurations, replacing the AC/20 with whatever weapons were available.

The recovery of lostech in the 3040s prompted Kali Yama to develop the HBK-5M upgrade under Free Worlds League Military contract, introducing double heat sinks and CASE protection but controversially reducing ammunition capacity. This flaw was brutally exposed during Operation Guerrero, where multiple advances stalled due to ammunition exhaustion. The lessons learned drove development of improved variants with greater ammunition stores and alternative armaments. Norse-Storm BattleMechs entered Hunchback production during the Jihad era, opening a refit line on Yed Posterior that quickly expanded to full manufacturing, contributing several innovative new variants including designs with jump capability and electronic warfare suites.

During the War of 3039, the Ninth Ghost Regiment experimented with mounting prototype Gauss rifles on Hunchback chassis at Elidere IV, but persistent balance problems forced reversion to the standard autocannon after the conflict. This episode illustrated both the enduring appeal of the Hunchback platform and the difficulty of fundamentally altering its proven design philosophy.

By the Dark Age era, the Hunchback remained in widespread service across all major powers, with Coventry Metal Works and Colonial Tractors joining the list of manufacturers. The design's longevity stands as evidence of the fundamental soundness of its original concept: a simple, rugged platform built around the biggest gun that could be fitted to a medium-weight chassis.

text.overview:
The HBK-LGN-Pin Ugly Stepsister Anastasia is a fifty-ton mixed-technology BattleMech fielded by the Solaris dueling stable Team Godmother during the Dark Age. Like its twin, it was not designed so much as assembled, pieced together from the salvaged remains of three unrelated 'Mechs into a single hybrid frame. The team presented it as one half of a matched pair of arena brawlers, cast in the role of a wicked stepsister to fit the stable's Cinderella theme.

Anastasia took the slower and heavier of the two roles. It is a deliberate close-range bruiser, trading speed and finesse for raw stopping power, and trusts thick protection to carry it into knife-fighting range against flashier opponents.
text.capabilities:
Anastasia is built around a single overwhelming alpha strike. A heavy large laser pairs with an autocannon/20 to deliver a punishing volume of damage at close range, and a targeting computer tightens the accuracy of both weapons so that those hits land where the pilot intends. Ten double heat sinks comfortably manage the energy weapon's heat, leaving the machine free to fire on the move without risk of shutdown.

The trade-offs are severe and deliberate. A standard two-hundred-rated fusion engine limits the 'Mech to a walking pace, making it one of the slower mediums in any arena and easy for nimbler opponents to circle. The autocannon carries only a single ton of ammunition, so its heaviest punch is exhausted quickly. Standard armor over the salvaged hybrid frame is generous for the tonnage but offers no special protection, leaving Anastasia reliant on closing the distance before its limited speed and ammunition become liabilities.
text.deployment: Within Team Godmother, Anastasia filled the anchor role, the heavy that opponents had to respect before committing. In the close confines of a Solaris arena its lack of speed mattered less, and its ability to cripple or kill with a single exchange made it dangerous to any duelist drawn into a brawl. Crowds knew it as the brute of the pair.

text.overview:
The HBK-LGN-Pin Ugly Stepsister Drizella is a fifty-ton mixed-technology BattleMech built for the Solaris dueling stable Team Godmother during the Dark Age. It is the twin counterpart to Anastasia, assembled from the same salvaged trio of donor 'Mechs and presented as the second of the team's wicked stepsisters under the stable's Cinderella theme.

Where its sister leans on mass and armor, Drizella takes the opposite approach. It is fast and light on its feet, built around mobility and a dense battery of short-range energy weapons rather than a single heavy punch. The design trades reach and durability for speed, aiming to close quickly and overwhelm a single opponent before the crowd has time to settle.
text.capabilities:
Drizella is a saturation brawler designed to bury a single target under a wall of short-range fire. Its mixed battery combines a pair of medium lasers, two Clan medium pulse lasers, and four Clan micro pulse lasers, a loadout that produces enormous damage at point-blank range while contributing almost nothing past a short reach. A three-hundred-fifty-rated extralight engine drives the machine to highway speeds, and jump jets let it cover nearly its full running distance in a single bound, giving it the agility to dictate range against slower foes.

That speed and firepower come at a cost. Fourteen double heat sinks struggle to keep pace with the full array, so the pilot must choose which weapons fire on any given pass or risk building dangerous heat. The extralight engine saves weight but spreads vulnerable components into the side torsos, and the short effective range of every weapon means a faster or longer-ranged opponent can simply refuse the close fight Drizella needs.
text.deployment: Drizella was Team Godmother's aggressor, using its speed and jump capability to chase down and corner single opponents in the arena. The machine excelled in the kind of fast, brutal, short-ranged duel its loadout was tuned for, swarming a target with overlapping fire before a bout could turn into a long-range contest. Spectators came to recognize it as the faster, flashier half of the Stepsister pairing.

text.overview: When Clan Jade Falcon recaptured Pandora from the Lyran Commonwealth they found their old production line building a new Hunchback IIC variant. Hoping to make a “sensible” Hunchback IIC, the Lyrans used pulse lasers and LB 20-X autocannons to maintain an improved heat curve while almost doubling the killing potential of their own Hunchbacks. With Red Devil Industries back in Falcon hands, the Hunchback IIC 5 is a common sight on the Steiner front. Its nature forces the Lyrans to employ Clan-like quick, decisive strikes.
text.notableUnits: Sergeant Brinella MacKenna: When Sergeant Brinella MacKenna returned to Arc-Royal after raiding Zanderij, she was assigned a Lyran Hunchback IIC to replace her gutted Gauntlet. A Kell Hound couldn’t be picky in early September 3146, so she drowned her sorrow in a bottle of whiskey. The next morning, she was dragged out of bed to reports of five Clusters of Falcons landing on-world. Given the limitations of her ’Mech, MacKenna was assigned to defend Old Connaught. In the second week, the Fifty-Third Falcon Talon hit. Her lance managed to grind through a Star of light ’Mechs when a black and green Shrike descended upon them. Two of her companions died in seconds. Out-massed, out-gunned, and outmaneuvered, MacKenna grappled the Shrike, pinning it to the ground and firing shell after shell into it. When her LB 20-Xs ran dry she ejected and hoped for the best, not knowing she was leaving a deeply fuming Khan Malvina Hazen on the ground.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A pairs a pair of large pulse lasers with an LRM-10 and LB 2-X autocannon, creating a loadout equally effective at range and in close quarters. The heavy firepower and similarity to the Crossbow B configuration have made it a MechWarrior favorite, particularly among Clan Steel Viper warriors who appreciate the consistent damage output at all engagement distances. Two additional double heat sinks manage the significant thermal load generated by the pulse lasers.

Alternate Configuration B centers on an ER PPC for long-range engagements, supported by an LB 10-X autocannon and paired medium pulse lasers at closer ranges. Two machine guns provide effective anti-infantry capability. This configuration demands patience from its MechWarrior, as pilots must carefully manage the transition between long-range sniping and close-range brawling. The B has been most commonly spotted with Clan Nova Cat forces, where warriors favor the cluster ammunition option of the LB-X autocannon for engaging fast-moving targets.

Alternate Configuration D utilizes an ATM-6 launcher with three tons of ammunition, allowing MechWarriors to adjust their missile payload as engagement ranges shift. An Ultra autocannon/10 provides substantial medium-range firepower, while paired medium pulse lasers and a small pulse laser deliver accurate close-range strikes. This configuration has been deployed as long-range missile support by several Clans, with the flexible ATM ammunition options proving particularly valuable in fluid battlefield situations.

Introduced during the Jihad era, Alternate Configuration E emphasizes accuracy through the use of pulse laser technology. A large pulse laser and paired medium pulse lasers deliver precise fire even while exploiting the Huntsman's jump capability, supported by an ATM-6 with three tons of ammunition and an ER small laser. A light active probe, light TAG, and anti-missile system provide electronic warfare capability. Four additional double heat sinks help manage the considerable thermal output, allowing sustained engagements without significant performance degradation.

A product of the Dark Age, Alternate Configuration F pairs an improved heavy large laser with two ER medium lasers, all linked to a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy. An Artemis V-equipped LRM-15 provides guided missile support at range. To manage the extreme heat generated by the improved heavy laser, the configuration mounts fourteen double heat sinks and a Radical Heat Sink System, though the latter introduces a degree of mechanical risk that some warriors find unacceptable in sustained operations.

Alternate Configuration G is built for aggressive close-quarters combat. A retractable blade in the right arm provides devastating melee capability, while three ER medium pulse lasers in the left arm and a leg-mounted small pulse laser deliver accurate energy weapon fire. Paired Streak SRM-6 launchers with CASE II-protected ammunition bays add reliable short-range missile firepower. A pod-mounted engine supercharger allows the Huntsman G to sprint at one hundred kilometers per hour in short bursts, closing to blade range with surprising speed. An active probe and targeting computer complete the package.

Alternate Configuration H serves as a powerful reconnaissance and electronic warfare platform. An active probe and ECM suite provide comprehensive detection and disruption capabilities, while an advanced targeting computer enhances the accuracy of the configuration's considerable arsenal. Paired ER large lasers deliver punishing long-range fire, supported by four heavy medium lasers and a heavy small laser for closer engagements. Six additional double heat sinks struggle to manage the extreme thermal load, making careful heat management essential for sustained operations.

Alternate Configuration I provides heavy fire support capability unusual for a medium OmniMech. A Hyper-Assault Gauss 20 in the right arm delivers devastating long-range kinetic strikes, fed by a three-ton ammunition bay. The left arm mounts an ER large laser and a plasma cannon with two tons of ammunition, offering flexible energy and area-denial capability. An ER small pulse laser handles close-in threats. This configuration allows the Huntsman to contribute meaningful firepower in engagements typically dominated by heavier designs.

Alternate Configuration N serves as a fusion of Warden and Crusader technological philosophies. An ER PPC and ER large laser provide formidable long-range direct-fire capability, enhanced by a targeting computer for improved accuracy. An ATM-6 offers flexible missile support, while a heavy medium laser adds weight at closer ranges. Three additional double heat sinks help manage the significant energy weapon heat output. This configuration has proven particularly effective in the hands of experienced warriors who can exploit the targeting computer's benefits at extended range.

A modern refresh introduced during the ilClan era, Alternate Configuration T provides a broad weapons mix reminiscent of the original Prime configuration. Each arm mounts a pair of improved heavy medium lasers for reliable close-range firepower, while an Ultra autocannon/2 and paired Streak LRM-5 launchers provide long-range harassment capability. A Streak SRM-6, micro pulse laser, ER small laser, and flamer round out the short-range arsenal, with a laser anti-missile system providing point defense. Each missile launcher and the autocannon carry a single ton of ammunition, demanding careful ammunition management in prolonged engagements.

text.overview: The Huron Warrior was designed by Hollis Incorporated on the Capellan Confederation world of Corey as a medium fire-support BattleMech. Originally conceived along similar lines to the Dervish or Trebuchet, the design underwent dramatic revision during the early 3050s as recovered Star League technology became increasingly available. Hollis engineers completely rethought the weapon payload, shifting from an indirect fire platform to a devastating direct-fire combatant. Introduced in 3055, the Huron Warrior filled a critical gap in the Confederation's medium 'Mech lineup, emphasizing long-range precision firepower in a fifty-ton package that could hold its own against heavier opponents. The design's effectiveness attracted interest from Trinity Alliance partners and select mercenary commands, expanding its operational footprint well beyond Capellan borders.
text.capabilities:
The Huron Warrior was redesigned to counter medium Clan OmniMechs such as the Black Hawk. Heavy armor and an XL engine gave Hollis's design resilience and agility while carrying an effective weapons load. The 'Mech's primary armament centers on a modified Grizzard Model 210 Gauss Rifle, providing devastating long-range striking power capable of stripping armor from even heavy targets in a single salvo. A Martell extended-range large laser supplements the main gun, ensuring the Huron Warrior can maintain punishing fire at engagement ranges where many opponents cannot effectively respond. A Martell medium pulse laser provides accurate close-range defense, though MechWarriors must manage their approach carefully as the 'Mech transitions between range brackets.

Ten tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provide solid protection for a fifty-ton chassis, giving the Huron Warrior the staying power to hold firing positions under return fire. The Magna 250 XL engine delivers a respectable top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, granting adequate battlefield mobility. One persistent criticism of the design involves the retention of standard heat sinks rather than double heat sinks, placing significant thermal management demands on pilots relying heavily on the laser armament. The lack of jump jets further limits tactical flexibility in complex terrain, though the Geometric 590 endo steel chassis helps offset the weight of the advanced weapons package.
text.deployment: Emerging in the early thirty-second century, this upgrade of the R4O replaces both the extended-range large laser and medium pulse laser along with one ton of ammunition and a hand actuator. The freed tonnage accommodates an XL gyro, stealth armor, a Guardian ECM suite, and a PPC fitted with a PPC capacitor. This configuration blends the Gauss Rifle's long-range punch with the PPC's versatility while making the Huron Warrior substantially more difficult to detect and engage at range.
text.battleHistory:
McCarron's Armored Cavalry was the first unit to receive the Huron Warrior, a preferential arrangement that contributed to that unit's decision to abandon its mercenary status and formally join the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. This early endorsement established the design's credentials within the CCAF's medium 'Mech doctrine, and the Huron Warrior quickly spread to frontline units throughout the Confederation.

The design's first true test under fire came during the conflict to reabsorb the St. Ives Compact. Fighting in the Compact revealed significant flaws in the Huron Warrior, as protracted combat exposed the 'Mech's reliance on standard heat sinks. While experienced MechWarriors could manage the thermal buildup from the laser armament, too many less experienced Capellan pilots struggled to operate effectively without the double heat sinks that had become standard in many contemporary designs.

Following the formation of the Trinity Alliance, the Huron Warrior expanded beyond the Confederation's borders. The Magistracy of Canopus fielded the design in its Canopian Light Horse regiments, while the Taurian Concordat equipped elements of the Pleiades Hussars with the 'Mech. House Marik's Second Sirian Lancers also ordered Huron Warriors to replace aging medium 'Mechs, and the Word of Blake acquired quantities of the design as part of its military buildup prior to the Jihad.

Mercenary commands have also fielded the Huron Warrior in limited numbers. During Operation Serpent, the Northwind Highlanders found the design's primary cannon to be an excellent anti-ProtoMech weapon during the invasion of Huntress, demonstrating the 'Mech's adaptability against targets far different from those originally envisioned by its creators.

The Huron Warrior has continued to evolve through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with the stealth-capable R4N and the upgraded R5L ensuring the design remains relevant on thirty-second century battlefields. Hollis Incorporated's continued investment in the platform reflects the Capellan Confederation's enduring commitment to maintaining a diverse and capable medium 'Mech force.

text.deployment: The production model represents the culmination of VEST's experience with earlier Kintaro-based prototypes. Powered by a standard fusion engine and equipped with industrial-grade armor, the HYN-4A carries the full complement of salvage equipment including dual lift hoists, a salvage arm, and environmental sealing. A single small laser provides token defensive capability. This variant established the Hyena's reputation during its brief production window, with every unit from the sole completed run selling immediately upon availability to mercenary commands, Great Houses, and Periphery nations alike.

After the destruction of VEST's primary production facilities in Xolara during 3072, engineers working from makeshift workshops managed to construct three units powered by internal combustion engines for the Solaris Home Defense League. The switch to an ICE powerplant reduced the maximum speed to 64 kilometers per hour, and the original small laser was replaced with a machine gun and one ton of ammunition, providing more practical anti-infantry capability for the planetary defense role. These units represented VEST's determination to continue supporting Solaris VII's defenders even after losing their primary manufacturing infrastructure.

text.deployment: Developed for the Republic of the Sphere and produced by Gilmour Miltech on Talitha, this variant stands as a radical reimagining of the Icarus II as an electronic warfare platform. The variant retains the original ICR-1S chassis and engine but completely replaces the conventional weapons suite with a pair of TSEMP cannons mounted in arms fitted with actuator enhancement systems for improved accuracy. A TAG system provides targeting data for allied indirect fire assets. The removal of all ballistic and energy weapons in favor of the twin TSEMPs transforms the Icarus II from a conventional striker into a specialized disruption platform capable of shutting down enemy 'Mechs through electromagnetic pulses. While devastating against isolated targets, the design lacks meaningful backup weaponry beyond a single ER small laser, making it heavily dependent on lance support.
text.battleHistory:
The Icarus II entered production at Corean Enterprises on Stewart in 2518 and quickly became the standard BattleMech of the Free Worlds League for decades. As one of the first 'Mechs to use modern production technology, it cemented its place in the lore of the Free Worlds League Military. At the height of its prominence, the design was produced on four separate worlds, including Oriente where Oriente Weapon Works operated a second production line. The march of technology gradually rendered the Icarus II obsolete as faster, more capable medium designs entered service. Before the creation of the Star League, three of the four facilities were retooled for newer designs, with the Corean plant on Stewart continuing until it was destroyed in the First Succession War.

Despite the loss of all production capacity, a small number of ICR-1S models survived the Succession Wars, primarily serving with provincial militias where replacement equipment was scarce. These aging machines persisted through centuries of conflict, a quiet proof of the fundamental soundness of Corean's engineering even if the design's combat relevance had long since faded.

The Icarus II experienced an unlikely renaissance during the Jihad. Gilmour Miltech, a small manufacturer on Talitha, began production of the modernized ICR-2S in 3073, producing only three units per year but representing the first new Icarus II models in over three centuries. Graham-Davis Enterprises on Tamarind soon followed with their own limited ICR-2S production, assisted by the government Venkateswara refit facility. These efforts met the desperate wartime demand for military hardware among forces cut off from larger manufacturers.

The Republic of the Sphere later recognized the Icarus II as a viable platform for advanced electronic warfare, with Gilmour Miltech producing the TSEMP-armed ICR-2R beginning in the Late Republic era. The Republic Institute of Strategic Combat pushed this concept further with the experimental ICR-2X mounting a repeating TSEMP, though the program was ultimately discontinued in favor of OmniMech-based TSEMP development.

In the ilClan era, Marian Arms on Alphard joined the ICR-1S and ICR-2S production network after upgrading from their earlier RetroTech Icarus lines with Graham-Davis assistance. A lone ICR-2X survived to see combat during the battle of Nagoya against Clan Jade Falcon forces, a fitting final chapter for one of the Inner Sphere's oldest BattleMech lineages.

text.deployment: This variant was developed by the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat beginning in 3135 at the RISC Proving Ground Fraternité on Terra. Built on the ICR-2S's endo-steel and XL engine platform rather than the original ICR-1S, the design replaces the twin TSEMPs of the ICR-2R with an experimental repeating TSEMP, one of the first 'Mechs to mount this weapon. Two medium pulse lasers linked to a targeting computer provide accurate backup firepower, supplemented by a small laser for close defense. Initial field trials saw the prototype deployed in covert operations, but engineering flaws in the repeating TSEMP proved impossible to correct on the Icarus platform. The RISC ultimately abandoned the design in favor of modular OmniMech configurations for further TSEMP development. The last surviving ICR-2X was pressed into service during the Clan invasion of Terra and saw action against Clan Jade Falcon forces, reportedly accounting for several disabled OmniMechs before the battle concluded.
